target: Close application-layer DNS rebinding and non-public destination SSRF gaps in the existing bridge poller without claiming network-namespace or egress-proxy isolation.

criteria.pass: Rust and an independent Python oracle agree on preregistered public and non-public IPv4/IPv6 known answers, including loopback, private, link-local, shared, benchmarking, documentation, multicast, reserved, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, Teredo, 6to4, ULA and non-global IPv6 cases.
The default CLI rejects a loopback HTTP URL before any TCP accept; the old binary connects and verifies the same served Outbox, while the new binary emits blocked_egress and zero server hits.
A hostname whose actual resolver answer is non-public is rejected before connection; an empty answer, excessive answer count or any non-public member of a mixed answer set fails closed.

The HTTP client performs exactly one policy resolution, dials only the validated SocketAddr set, preserves the original URL authority in the HTTP Host header, and never invokes a scripted second resolution.
A deliberately blocked resolver exceeds its small remaining budget without blocking the caller or dialing an HTTP server; the residual resolver worker cannot itself initiate HTTP.
Session JSON cannot enable non-public egress because unknown fields remain rejected; only an explicit process-level test/legacy option can construct the allow-non-public poller.
Existing file transport, public-address classification, chain verification, execution fixtures and whole-poll deadline behavior remain valid, and a clean archive rebuild passes the complete gate.

not_proven: No claim of kernel/network-namespace egress enforcement, protection against a hostile OS or non-cooperative process, complete DNS resolver cancellation, or universal SSRF prevention outside this HTTP client.
No new publisher authentication, remote Git synchronization, QF-OS canonical compatibility, QIOS compatibility, zero-knowledge proof or distributed exactly-once claim.
